reading.thesis: This is a mono-green deck that spends the three turns which are not yours: Radagast opens one discounted flash window per player turn, a creature walks through each one, a card-per-body engine pays for the creature, and the accumulated board is cashed in by a mass-pump finisher — whose verified kill threshold is FIVE other bodies beside the finisher, not the finisher itself.

lines.name: fuel → conversion
lines.note: The only place bodies are consumed for cards, and the deck does not choose it: under an opponent's Day of Judgment you draw 4, because the Insect token's zone-change trigger fires before it ceases to exist and indestructible Toski skips the wake. This is what a fodder stage would look like if the deck had one.

lines.name: ignition → conversion
lines.note: Retargeted from iteration 1's fuel->output, which contained none of its via cards. Ohran Frostfang has no printed flash: the window is what puts it on the battlefield after blockers, where its static deathtouch applies to damage already lined up, and one unblocked 1/1 then draws exactly 2 off Frostfang and Toski together.

lines.name: fuel → wincon
lines.note: THE FLOOR. Four other bodies under the Hoof is X=5 and 36 unblocked into 40 — the seat survives on 4. This board does not win.

lines.name: fuel → wincon
lines.note: THE THRESHOLD, and it is the next body up. Five other bodies under the Hoof, cast in your own precombat main, is X=6 and exactly 40 trample power into one seat — lethal with no margin at all, and only ever to one seat.

open_questions.question: Whiptongue Hydra flashed in after blockers are declared: does its ETB sweep the fliers before combat damage, how many +1/+1 counters does it keep, and does it kill your own Hornet Nest tokens and Hornet Queen tokens in the process?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the deck's premise card — a six-mana creature with no printed flash that is only an answer because the window makes it one — and no answer effect in the output stage is verified by any passing stack — Chord of Calling (007) is the stage's one verified member and it tutors rather than answers. The premise is unverified, and the collateral question is live: Hornet Nest and Hornet Queen both make 1/1 fliers, and Arasta makes reach Spiders that would survive.

open_questions.question: Can Scute Swarm alone reach the fifth body BESIDE the finisher? With six or more lands its landfall creates a copy of itself per land entering; how many bodies does the board hold on the turn before Craterhoof, counting one land drop plus a fetch from Wood Elves or Sakura-Tribe Elder?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 003 measured four other bodies plus Craterhoof at 36 into 40 — not lethal — and stack 005 measured five other bodies plus Craterhoof at exactly 40. The gap between the two is one body, and Scute Swarm is the only card in the 71 that manufactures bodies without spending a window. It is the deck's cheapest route to the one threshold a verified stack has already priced.

open_questions.question: Does Mirkwood Pathmaker function as this deck's greatest-power dial? With N lands, what is the X on Overwhelming Stampede and Pathbreaker Ibex, how many cards does Return of the Wildspeaker draw, and does Selvala's 'power greater than each other creature's power' gate then shut off for every subsequent body — including against opponents' creatures?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Three of the four finishers, the finisher-that-is-really-a-draw-spell and the deck's single priced point of failure all multiply by one number, and one card sets it. No declared component groups them, no passing stack touches it, and the map has it only four-fifths right. It is also the one place where the coupling may run backwards: Selvala's gate compares against EACH OTHER creature's power, opponents' included, so a large Pathmaker could suppress her draw trigger for the rest of the game.

open_questions.question: Over the board this deck actually assembles, do the other three finishers close? Specifically: on stack 003's exact board (Radagast 2/5, Scute Swarm 1/1, Wood Elves 1/1, Beast Whisperer 2/3, seven lands), what does Overwhelming Stampede deal, what does Pathbreaker Ibex deal on the turn after it attacks, and what does Return of the Wildspeaker's +3/+3 mode deal given three Humans in the 71?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This replaces a withdrawn claim. Iteration 1 called Craterhoof the wincon stage's single point of failure; the audit prices the class as four interchangeable cards at 42.4% by t6, and nothing in this deck's seven passing stacks resolves any of the other three. Both readings — 'the four are one class' and 'Craterhoof is the deck' — are currently unevidenced, and one number decides it: what X is without a Craterhoof on the board, since Stampede and Ibex read greatest power and Craterhoof reads creature count.

open_questions.question: Does the protection stage hold up the two ways it will actually be attacked? (a) Saryth grants hexproof to OTHER UNTAPPED creatures you control — is an attacking Radagast, and Saryth herself, targetable by a removal spell during combat? (b) Guardian Augmenter grants commanders hexproof, not indestructible — does Radagast survive a Day of Judgment, and if he does not, does Heroic Intervention's indestructible cover the rest of a board the wrath is aimed at?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Eight cards in this deck exist to make one removal spell not be the whole game, and not one of them appears in the scenario of any passing stack. The stage is evidenced by a map city and by oracle text alone. Both sub-questions are cases where the printed wording is narrower than the job the stage is filed under, which is exactly the shape of coaching error that propagates. The Sylvan Safekeeper half of (b) is WITHDRAWN rather than asked: shroud is 'can't be the target of spells or abilities' (702.18a) and a wrath targets nothing, so the card text settles it and it is not worth a stack spawn.

open_questions.question: Glademuse reads 'whenever a player casts a spell, if it's not their turn, THAT PLAYER draws a card.' Against a pod with instant-speed decks, does this deck net ahead on it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The strategic frame calls Glademuse 'tuned to this deck exactly'. The oracle text is symmetric and pays whoever casts, so the claim is really that this deck casts off-turn more than the table does. That is a claim about the format, not about the card, and nothing in the artifacts checks it.

open_questions.question: How much of the metronome's real output is the simulator missing? The declaration's own note says the sim models neither Radagast's discount, nor aura ramp (Utopia Sprawl, Wild Growth, Fertile Ground), nor opponent-turn flash casts.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every rate quoted in this model — 94.5%, 93.6%, 91.3%, 75.9%, 63.0%, 42.4%, 40.2%, 12.3% — is a floor for a deck whose entire design is the three things not being modelled, and the size of the gap is unknown. Three columnists will quote these figures; they should know which direction they are wrong in.

findings.claim: 'it is about the SIX mana-stage creatures that actually tap for mana (Birds of Paradise, Devoted Druid, Elvish Mystic, Fyndhorn Elves, Llanowar Elves, Scaled Nurturer), seven if you count Elvish Reclaimer, whose land fetch also costs {T}; Tireless Provisioner has no activated ability of its own and Elvish Spirit Guide is exiled from hand, so 302.6 never gates either. This stack names none of them.'
findings.note: REPAIR 1 ACCEPTED, and it is exact rather than approximately right. I did not take round 2's enumeration on trust; I recomputed the set from cards.json against stages[0].cards. Filtering the mana stage's ten creatures for a '{T}: Add' ability returns Birds of Paradise, Elvish Mystic, Llanowar Elves, Fyndhorn Elves, Devoted Druid and Scaled Nurturer — the six named, in the same set, with nothing omitted and nothing added, so the count is COMPLETE for the scope it declares and not merely smaller than eight. Each exclusion is right on the printed text: Tireless Provisioner is 'Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, create a Food token or a Treasure token', a triggered ability, and the {T} in its text belongs to the Treasure's REMINDER text, not to Provisioner (a naive regex is fooled here and the model is not); Elvish Spirit Guide is 'Exile this card from your hand: Add {G}', activated from hand, so 302.6 — which restricts a tap symbol in an activation cost of a permanent that has not been controlled since the turn began — never reaches it. The Reclaimer hedge is right too and the hedge is the correct form: '{2}, {T}, Sacrifice a land' does carry a tap symbol, so 302.6 gates it, but it fetches a land rather than adding mana, which is exactly why it is 'seven if you count' rather than seven. Final clause holds: 006's scenario names only Radagast and Sakura-Tribe Elder, so 'this stack names none of them' is true. ROUND 2 PROPOSED A MECHANICAL CHECK HERE AND IT SHOULD BE BUILT: when a note attributes a 302.6 finding to a named set, assert every member has a tap symbol in an activation cost in cards.json. It passes on all seven named cards now and would have failed on the old eight. One implementation warning from running it: strip parenthesised reminder text first, or Tireless Provisioner false-PASSES the check the sentence correctly excludes it from.

findings.claim: 'no ANSWER from this stage is verified by any passing stack — Chord of Calling (007) is the stage's one verified member and it tutors rather than answers'
findings.note: REPAIR 2 ACCEPTED. I re-derived the negative rather than accepting round 2's version of it, and it is stronger than the sentence claims. Intersecting stages[4].cards (all ten) against the FULL TEXT of all seven stacks — not just the scenario boards — the only hit in the corpus is Chord of Calling, in 007. Nantuko Vigilante, Wickerbough Elder, Indrik Stomphowler, Whiptongue Hydra, Caustic Caterpillar, Ravenous Sailback, Beast Within, Pick Your Poison and Collector Ouphe appear nowhere, in no scenario, no step and no checker note. All seven stacks are checker-passed. 'It tutors rather than answers' is what 007 actually does with it: X=3, convoking three creatures, searching for Selvala, Heart of the Wilds, with the stack's four claims being three negatives about Radagast's discount, Garenbrig's restricted six and Beast Whisperer's trigger, plus the positive that Selvala may tap on your following turn. No destroy, no disable, no answer effect resolves. The absolute is now bounded by the one counter-example it previously ran over, which is the whole repair. This is MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE and cheap: a stage note asserting 'no member of this stage is verified' should be tested by intersecting stages[i].cards with the union of card names in every passing stack, and any hit must be named in the sentence — which is what this sentence now does.

findings.claim: 'no answer effect in the output stage is verified by any passing stack — Chord of Calling (007) is the stage's one verified member and it tutors rather than answers'
findings.note: The same repair, made in the second place round 2 found the absolute, with the same qualifier and the same named exception. This is the copy that matters most: open_questions[0] is one of the three the Game Plan's not-modelled rail can print, so it is the sentence with a route to the page, and it no longer states an absolute a reader could refute by reading the stage's own next evidence entry. Both copies now carry the exception, so a future edit to one and not the other is visible as a divergence.

findings.claim: the two repairs are the only edits; nothing else moved
findings.note: Verified mechanically rather than by reading. I diffed the working file against HEAD (commit 827a69a) key-by-key with the top-level `critic` block excluded, recursing into every stage, line, rebuttal, disagreement, open question and proposed edit. Exactly THREE leaf strings changed — lines[1].note, stages[4].evidence[0].note, open_questions[0].why_it_matters — and they are the two repairs. No key added, no key removed, no list length changed, no number touched. Everything round 2 confirmed is byte-identical to what it confirmed: lines[8]'s founding on 005 step 7, the six-mana-pool inference, the lines[1] rebuttal, the null ignition SPOF, all nine `carries` nouns, the eight goldfish rates, the four city scatters, the five map_disagreements and the seven null single_point_of_failure fields. `manamap pilot validate-engine radagast` returns OK — 7 stages, 71 cards placed, 0 unassigned, 9/9 lines verified by a passing stack. There is no dashed line in this model, so the over-claiming-note class has nothing to fire on this round.

findings.claim: implicitly, that the SIX is the relevant set for the 006 step 5 {T} finding
findings.note: Recorded so a later round does not read the six as a deck-wide count and 'fix' it. Deck-wide there is a SEVENTH creature that taps for mana — Selvala, Heart of the Wilds, '{G}, {T}: Add X mana in any combination of colors' — which this model files under conversion, not mana. The note is explicitly scoped to 'mana-stage creatures' and the arrow it annotates is ignition -> mana, so the stage scoping is the correct one and the sentence is not incomplete. Worth knowing, though, that the general {T} half is not only unverified-by-006 but is verified ELSEWHERE on a card the deck actually runs: stack 007 step 8 resolves exactly this boundary — 'Selvala entered during opponent 3's end step and you are next in turn order... her {G}, {T} ability is therefore activatable on your turn' — and 007's own note_for_the_resolver calls it 'the stack 006 boundary'. That does not change this line's disposition (the arrow's cards are Radagast and Sakura-Tribe Elder, and 006 is the right citation for the ramp-body prong), but it means the finding the note is careful not to over-attribute has a passing home.

findings.claim: 'the stage answers with two native instants' (Beast Within and Chord of Calling) against 'Chord of Calling... tutors rather than answers'
findings.note: CONSIDERED AND NOT CHARGED, with the reasoning recorded so it is not re-opened. The two sentences sit in one stage object and use 'answers' at different altitudes: what_it_does counts instant-speed DEPLOYMENT slots the stage can hold up without a grant (Chord genuinely is one, and a Chord for Indrik Stomphowler is an answer arriving at instant speed), while the evidence note is scoped to what a passing stack VERIFIES, and in 007 Chord fetches a mana creature and answers nothing. Neither statement asserts an unverified flow, and the narrowed one errs conservative — it understates Chord rather than crediting it with a resolution no stack shows. Charging this would be asking the model to weaken a true sentence about the deck in order to match a true sentence about the evidence, which is the opposite of the contract.

findings.claim: ignition -> wincon via Radagast of Rhosgobel + Craterhoof Behemoth, verified_by 005, carries 'the {2} discount': 'Stack 005 step 2 sets Craterhoof's total cost at {3}{G}{G}{G}... step 7 makes the identical payment in your own precombat main, which is the line that kills for exactly 40.'
findings.note: ANSWERED, and re-founded on a prong the stack does carry. I read step 7 rather than the model's account of it: its action is 'cast Craterhoof in your own precombat main phase with the identical mana (four Forests pay Garenbrig's {2}{G}{G}, Garenbrig's six {G} pay the discounted {3}{G}{G}{G})' — the word 'discounted' is the stack's, not the model's — and its effect reaches '11+8+7+7+7 = 40 power with trample... that player's life is 0'. Step 2 is the reduction itself ({5}{G}{G}{G} minus {2} = {3}{G}{G}{G} under 601.2f). Both steps' citations are checker 'supported', including 508.1a whose note re-verifies the pumped totals independently. So the discount prong is inside the only lethal line 005 measures, and the arrow now labels that prong. THE ENGINEER'S OWN INFERENCE CHECKS OUT: 005's pool is four untapped Forests plus Castle Garenbrig, and Garenbrig's oracle (cards.json) offers '{T}: Add {G}' or '{2}{G}{G}, {T}: Add six {G}'. The three available lines are 4 mana (Forests only), 5 (three Forests + Garenbrig's plain {G} — the activation needs all four), or 6 (four Forests bought into the six restricted {G}). Six is the maximum, undiscounted Craterhoof is {5}{G}{G}{G} = eight, so it is uncastable on that board and the discount is load-bearing rather than incidental. The note flags the arithmetic as its own and it is right. The flash refutation is now one clause saying what the arrow does NOT claim, and the refutation itself still lives in stages[6].what_it_does where it is correct.

findings.where: lines[1] (the rebuttal against re-citing onto a mana dork)
findings.claim: rebuttals[7]: 'The critic's second remedy, move the tap prong onto a via card that has a tap ability, has no stack to cite — Birds, Llanowar Elves and Devoted Druid appear in no passing scenario... withdrawing the arrow would throw away a flow 006 does verify.'
findings.note: The rebuttal is correct on both legs and I checked it rather than conceding it. Leg one: I enumerated every passing scenario's cards with build_index.line_cards against the 71 — 001 {Radagast, Wood Elves}, 002 {Llanowar Elves, Ohran Frostfang, Radagast, Toski}, 003 {Beast Whisperer, Castle Garenbrig, Craterhoof, Radagast, Scute Swarm, Wood Elves}, 004 {Fecundity, Radagast, Scute Swarm, Toski, Wood Elves}, 005 {Castle Garenbrig, Craterhoof, Hornet Nest, Radagast, Scute Swarm, Toski, Wood Elves}, 006 {Radagast, Sakura-Tribe Elder}, 007 {Beast Whisperer, Castle Garenbrig, Chord of Calling, Llanowar Elves, Radagast, Wood Elves}. Llanowar Elves IS on 002's board, so one dork does appear — but only as an attacking 1/1 whose damage triggers the draws; 002 never activates a mana ability and its arrow is already drawn (lines[4], ignition -> conversion). No scenario activates any dork's {T}, so a re-cited ignition -> mana arrow through Birds/Mystic/Druid would name cards no stack resolves, which is the mis-citation the round-1 findings existed to stop. Leg two: 006 does verify a mana-stage card reaching the battlefield through the window (step 1, cast for {G} under Radagast's reduction; the checker's step-1 note confirms '{1}{G} minus a {2} reduction correctly leaves {G}'), and the authored carries says 'a ramp body', not mana. Keeping the arrow and narrowing the note was the right disposition.

findings.claim: 'The general {T} half IS verified at step 5 — an end-step arrival may activate a {T} ability on your turn — but it is about the eight dorks in the mana stage, none of which this stack names.'
findings.note: THE ONE DEFECT THIS ROUND, and it is new: it sits in the very sentence written to answer round-1 findings[4], which is the fix-one-break-one pattern this deck is on record for. 006 step 5's {T} finding cannot be about eight cards, because two of the eight have no tap ability at all. findings.claim: ignition -> wincon via Radagast of Rhosgobel + Craterhoof Behemoth, verified_by 005. Note: 'The one card the window is wrong for. Flashed on the prior end step, the +6/+6 and trample end at that turn's cleanup (514.2) and the swing is 10 unpumped power.'
findings.note: The refuted-flow defect is back, one layer subtler, and it is the reason for the fail. This arrow has a non-null verified_by, so the renderer draws it SOLID GREEN — proof — and it has no `carries`, so design.line_carries falls through to STAGE_CARRIES['ignition'] = 'windows' and publishes an italic label reading 'windows' on an arrow from ignition to wincon. Stack 005 establishes the opposite of that label. Step 5: 'The pump and trample expire before your turn ever begins. There is no window in which a pumped board of yours and your combat phase coexist.' Step 6: '10 total power, no trample, no pump... The end-step-flash line does NOT kill.' final_state: 'the flash cast is simply wasted defense on a turn nobody attacks you.' A reader of the schematic sees ignition proven to deliver windows into the win condition; the cited stack shows that route killing nobody. Crucially there IS a surviving ignition -> wincon flow and the note never names it: step 7 casts Craterhoof in your own precombat main 'for the discounted {3}{G}{G}{G}', i.e. Radagast's {2} reduction — the OTHER prong of the same ability — is what the win line actually consumes. The remedy is not to delete the arrow but to make it about the prong the stack carries: author `carries: "the {2} discount"` and rewrite the note around step 7, keeping the flash refutation where it already lives correctly (stages[6].what_it_does and stages[6].evidence[1]). This is NOT mechanically checkable and should not be attempted with string matching — 'the window is wrong for this card' is a sentence a correct model could also write; what makes it wrong here is that it sits under a solid arrow asserting the window.

findings.claim: neither line authors a `carries`, so both take a derived noun from STAGE_CARRIES keyed on the SOURCE stage
findings.note: These are the model's only two BACKWARD arrows (validate_engine.STAGES orders mana 0, ignition 1, fuel 2, fodder 3, conversion 4, output 5, protection 6, wincon 7; ignition->mana is 1->0 and wincon->conversion is 7->4), and derivation from the source stage is wrong for both by construction. lines[2] wincon->conversion will publish 'damage' — but nothing about damage reaches the conversion stage in stack 003: Beast Whisperer's trigger resolves at step 2, before Craterhoof has even resolved at step 3, and the 36 combat damage happens at step 7 and feeds nothing. What flows is a CARD. lines[1] ignition->mana will publish 'windows' flowing INTO the mana stage; what actually flows is a body, and what comes back is mana. A feedback loop by definition does not carry the source stage's own output backwards, which is exactly why STAGE_CARRIES cannot serve one. THIS ONE IS MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE and should become a permanent check: validate_engine should require an authored `carries` on any line whose `to` stage precedes its `from` stage in STAGES. On radagast it fires on exactly the two lines whose derived nouns are wrong and on none of the seven forward arrows.

findings.claim: 'A body flashed on an opponent's end step meets both prongs of 302.6 by your untap: it attacks and it taps freely.' via Radagast of Rhosgobel + Sakura-Tribe Elder, verified_by 006
findings.note: Half of this is exactly what 006 verifies and half of it is vacuous for the one card the line names. Stack 006 step 5 precision note (b): Sakura-Tribe Elder's ability 'Sacrifice this creature: Search your library for a basic land card...' 'has no tap or untap symbol in its cost, so 302.6 never restricted it at all' — confirmed against cards.json. So 'it taps freely' is true of the eight dorks in stages[0] and is empty of content for the via card. Worse for an arrow whose `to` stage is mana: 006 never produces any mana. findings.claim: 'The other seven (Nantuko Vigilante, Wickerbough Elder, Indrik Stomphowler, Whiptongue Hydra, Caustic Caterpillar, Ravenous Sailback, Collector Ouphe) have no printed flash and reach instant speed only through a flash grant... on Radagast alone the stage still answers with two native instants plus one granted creature per turn'
findings.note: The word 'only' is false for three of the seven, and the follow-on count is therefore a floor rather than the number it is stated as. From cards.json: Wickerbough Elder is '{G}, Remove a -1/-1 counter from this creature: Destroy target artifact or enchantment' and Caustic Caterpillar is '{1}{G}, Sacrifice this creature: Destroy target artifact or enchantment' — both ACTIVATED abilities, usable at instant speed from the battlefield with no flash grant and no window consumed. Nantuko Vigilante is 'Morph {1}{G} (...Turn it face up any time for its morph cost.)' with 'When this creature is turned face up, destroy target artifact or enchantment' — an instant-speed answer via morph, again no grant. Only the four whose answer is an ETB or a static (Indrik Stomphowler, Whiptongue Hydra, Ravenous Sailback, Collector Ouphe) genuinely depend on the flash grant for their timing. The stage conflates DEPLOYMENT timing with ANSWER timing, and the stage's own label is 'ANSWERS THAT COME DOWN AT INSTANT SPEED'. Note for the record how this survived round 3: the previous critic's exhaustiveness check grepped oracle text for 'flash' and 'any time you could cast an instant', which cannot see a morph reminder or an activated ability — so the sweep that pronounced the two grants 'the complete set' was blind to the three cards in this very stage that need no grant at all.

findings.claim: 'Sylvan Safekeeper, Heroic Intervention, Tyvar's Stand, Veil of Summer, Inspiring Call and Warg Tactics are held, not cast, which costs nothing here because the deck was holding mana anyway.'
findings.note: One of the six named cards is not an instant. cards.json gives Sylvan Safekeeper as '{G} | Creature — Human Wizard | Sacrifice a land: Target creature you control gains shroud until end of turn.' It cannot be 'held' the way the other five are — it must be CAST, at sorcery speed unless it is the turn's first creature spell through Radagast's window — and its protection ability costs a land sacrifice, not mana, so 'costs nothing here because the deck was holding mana anyway' is wrong about it in both halves. The other five are Instants and the sentence is correct about them (verified: Heroic Intervention {1}{G}, Tyvar's Stand {X}{G}, Veil of Summer {G}, Inspiring Call {2}{G}, Warg Tactics {1}{G}). This matters beyond pedantry because open_questions[4](b) already asks whether Safekeeper's shroud helps against a wrath; a pilot who has read this stage believes he can hold it up, and he cannot. It is also mechanically checkable: a card described as held/instant-speed-from-hand whose cards.json type_line contains 'Creature' and whose oracle text has no 'Flash'.

findings.claim: 'Radagast of Rhosgobel' is the ignition stage's single point of failure

She is narrower on exactly one axis: no cost reduction.' Yeva is in the 71 and in this stage's own cards array, so the qualifier 'and only if Yeva is one of the 71' is satisfied. Second, independent reason: Radagast is the commander, and stack 004 verifies at step 5 (903.9a, checker 'supported') that he returns to the command zone after dying, so he is the one card in the deck that removal cannot permanently answer. unmatched_v1_lines.note: Cast on an opponent's turn for {G}: the discount and the flash both applied because Wood Elves was that turn's first creature spell. One window per turn, four per round.

The window buys ramp with mana that would otherwise pass unspent: stack 006 casts Sakura-Tribe Elder for {G} on opponent 3's end step (Radagast's reduction, step 1), and by your untap 302.6 is satisfied so the body may attack (step 4). NARROWED to the attack prong: step 5(b) records that the Elder's 'Sacrifice this creature' cost has no tap or untap symbol, 'so 302.6 never restricted it at all', and 006 fetches no land and makes no mana. The general {T} half IS verified at step 5 — an end-step arrival may activate a {T} ability on your turn — but it is about the SIX mana-stage creatures that actually tap for mana (Birds of Paradise, Devoted Druid, Elvish Mystic, Fyndhorn Elves, Llanowar Elves, Scaled Nurturer), seven if you count Elvish Reclaimer, whose land fetch also costs {T}; Tireless Provisioner has no activated ability of its own and Elvish Spirit Guide is exiled from hand, so 302.6 never gates either. This stack names none of them.

The one backward arrow into the engine, and what flows back is a CARD, not damage: stack 003 step 1 has the cast of Craterhoof trigger Beast Whisperer, and step 2 resolves the draw — before the finisher itself resolves at step 3. The 36 combat damage happens at step 7 and feeds nothing. The turn the deck tries to win, it also draws.

Garenbrig's six {G} is spend-restricted to creature spells, which is why a land that would be a liability in most decks is the best one here. RE-CITED from 003: that stack pays for Craterhoof out of six Forests and leaves Garenbrig untapped, so the arrow asserted a flow its own stack showed not happening. Stack 005 verifies the flow end to end — four Forests buy the activation, the six restricted {G} pay the discounted {3}{G}{G}{G}, and the same restriction is what stops it paying for Chord in 007. validate-engine cannot catch this: both via cards sit in 003's scenario and in the right endpoint stages, so the mechanical gate passes while the citation is wrong.

PRICE, not timing — this arrow is about the discount prong and not the flash prong. Stack 005 step 2 sets Craterhoof's total cost at {3}{G}{G}{G}, six mana, 'minus all cost reductions' (601.2f), and step 3 pays it with Castle Garenbrig's six restricted {G}; step 7 makes the identical payment in your own precombat main, which is the line that kills for exactly 40. The scenario's entire pool is four Forests plus Garenbrig, whose best line is those same six, so undiscounted Craterhoof at {5}{G}{G}{G} is not castable on that board at all — the arithmetic is mine, read off the scenario's stated mana, not a checker verdict. The flash prong does NOT reach the win and this line does not claim it does: flashed on the prior end step the pump expires at cleanup (514.2) and the swing is 10 unpumped power, which is recorded under the wincon stage where it belongs.

v1_stages.label: MANA YOU DO NOT SPEND
v1_stages.what_it_does: Thirty-six deliberately plain lands plus a two-humped ramp class (18 cards, RAMP drawn by t6 at 93.6%) — but the job is not casting bigger things sooner. The job is having something left over when it is somebody else's turn. A tapped-out Radagast deck has three dead windows a round, so this stage is measured by what stays UNSPENT. Castle Garenbrig is the emblem: its six {G} burst is spend-restricted to creature spells, which makes a liability elsewhere the best land here. It APPEARS in three passing stacks (003, 005, 007) and it PAYS in exactly one of them — stack 005, where four Forests buy the activation and all six restricted {G} land on a discounted Craterhoof. In 003 the six Forests pay for Craterhoof directly and Garenbrig is explicitly left untapped; in 007 it cannot pay for Chord at all. An appearance count is not a load-bearing count, and iterations 1 and 2 reported it as one. Sakura-Tribe Elder, Elvish Reclaimer and Wood Elves sit on both sides of the ramp/body line; Wood Elves is filed under fuel because it is the canonical window body.

v1_stages.label: FOUR WINDOWS A ROUND
v1_stages.what_it_does: Radagast has to resolve. His one ability — 'the first creature spell you cast each turn costs {2} less to cast and can be cast as though it had flash' — grants the turn's FIRST creature spell both prongs at once, and 'each turn' means every player's turn: four windows per round in a four-player pod, verified. The two prongs have different backups, and that is why this stage names NO single point of failure. On TIMING, Yeva reads 'you may cast green creature spells as though they had flash' with no per-turn limit and this deck is mono-green, so she is strictly broader than Radagast; and Radagast is the commander, the one card removal cannot answer for good — stack 004 step 5 moves him to the command zone under 903.9a, recastable at tax. On PRICE there is no backup at all: nothing else in the 71 reduces a creature spell by {2}, and Yeva is a single copy that no declared component prices. Answering Radagast therefore does not answer the window — it answers the discount, and the discount is what the one verified kill payment is made of.

v1_stages.label: ONE BODY PER WINDOW
v1_stages.what_it_does: The window consumes one creature per turn, and the declared METRONOME component — 19 cards, drawn by t6 in 94.5% of runs, mean turn 1.615 — is what it eats. The declaration labels that component '3-5 MV, >=2 generic — the full-value flash-in class', and four of its nineteen members fall outside the stated band: Satyr Wayfinder ({1}{G}, MV 2, one generic), Eternal Witness ({1}{G}{G}, MV 3, one generic), Whiptongue Hydra (MV 6) and Hornet Queen (MV 7). The membership is defensible — all four are still bodies the window can deploy — but the parenthetical does not describe it, and a goldfish edit is proposed for that. The ten cards listed HERE are the narrower set whose only job is to be a body at the right price. Mirkwood Pathmaker is the odd one and the important one: its power and toughness each equal the number of lands you control, which makes it the deck's greatest-power dial — see map_disagreements.

v1_stages.label: A CARD PER BODY
v1_stages.what_it_does: The engine proper: it turns bodies into cards, which become bodies. Eleven cards are filed here; ten of them are the declared GAS component (drawn by t6 at 75.9%, mean turn 2.467) and the eleventh, Fauna Shaman, belongs to the declared TUTOR component instead — it converts a spare creature in hand into the specific one. What the engine converts is a resource other decks throw away: mana still untapped when the turn passes. Glademuse is the purest statement of that ('whenever a player casts a spell, if it's not their turn, that player draws') and it is symmetric. There is no `fodder` stage in this deck — not because nothing sacrifices (Sakura-Tribe Elder, Caustic Caterpillar, Sylvan Safekeeper and Elvish Reclaimer all do, and Tireless Provisioner makes Food and Treasure to crack), but because none of it is a THEME: no card here eats a body for value on purpose, and the one board that gets consumed in a passing stack is consumed by an opponent's Day of Judgment. Selvala is the deck's only priced single point of failure — a one-card class at 12.3% by t6 — though stack 007 shows Chord finds her at instant speed.

v1_stages.label: ANSWERS THAT COME DOWN AT INSTANT SPEED
v1_stages.what_it_does: What the window produces besides bodies: interaction on somebody else's turn, mostly wearing a creature. The declared FLASH TRAP component is 16 cards drawn by t6 at 91.3%, and it spans FIVE stages, 6/6/2/1/1: six here, six in protection, two in fuel (Hornet Nest, Dawn's Light Archer), one in conversion (Ohran Frostfang), one in ignition (Yeva). Two of the ten are native instants — Beast Within, and Chord of Calling, which stack 007 casts in opponent 3's end step under 304.1 while verifying that it takes no discount, consumes no window, cannot spend Garenbrig's restricted six and triggers no Beast Whisperer. One cannot be held at all: Pick Your Poison, a sorcery. The other seven split on WHEN THEY ANSWER, not on when they arrive. Three answer at instant speed from the battlefield with no grant and no window spent: Wickerbough Elder ('{G}, Remove a -1/-1 counter from this creature: Destroy target artifact or enchantment'), Caustic Caterpillar ('{1}{G}, Sacrifice this creature:' the same) and Nantuko Vigilante, whose morph reminder reads 'Turn it face up any time for its morph cost' and whose destroy trigger fires on the turn-up. Only four have the answer welded to the arrival — Indrik Stomphowler, Whiptongue Hydra and Ravenous Sailback on an ETB, Collector Ouphe on a static — and those four are the ones a flash grant times. For the other three a grant buys deployment, not timing. So on Radagast alone the stage answers with two native instants, one granted arrival a turn, and whatever of the three self-timers is already down; Yeva's grant has no per-turn limit.

v1_stages.label: THE INSURANCE ON ONE WIZARD
v1_stages.what_it_does: The deck is linear on Radagast and on one board, so this stage is what stops a single removal spell or a single wrath from being the whole game. Guardian Augmenter flashes in, pumps commander creatures +2/+2 and grants commanders hexproof; Saryth grants hexproof to OTHER untapped creatures you control and deathtouch to OTHER tapped ones — the 'other' matters twice, because Saryth protects neither herself nor a creature that has attacked, and an attacking Radagast is tapped and therefore uncovered. FIVE of the eight are instants held rather than cast: Heroic Intervention {1}{G}, Tyvar's Stand {X}{G}, Veil of Summer {G}, Inspiring Call {2}{G}, Warg Tactics {1}{G} — which costs nothing here because the deck was holding mana anyway. Sylvan Safekeeper is not the sixth and this model counted it as one: it is a {G} Human Wizard, so it has to be CAST, at sorcery speed unless it is that turn's first creature spell and spends the window on a 1/1 — and its protection is an activated ability paid in LAND, 'Sacrifice a land: Target creature you control gains shroud until end of turn'. It answers at instant speed only once it is already on the battlefield, and shroud is a targeting restriction (702.18a: 'can't be the target of spells or abilities'), so it does nothing against a wrath. Toski belongs functionally in this stage too and is filed under conversion; its indestructibility is verified in stack 004 and its draw in 002.

v1_stages.label: FIVE BODIES AND THE HOOF
v1_stages.what_it_does: A mass-pump alpha strike over a wide board. Four finishers, drawn by t6 at 42.4%; the declared ASSEMBLED target measures 40.2% — and its second group is TWENTY cards, the metronome nineteen plus Scute Swarm, not the metronome component its label names. Two passing stacks bracket the real threshold and it is the most important arithmetic in the deck. Stack 003: Craterhoof over FOUR other bodies is X=5, five attackers, 36 unblocked into a 40-life seat — NOT lethal, the seat survives on 4. Stack 005: Craterhoof cast in your own precombat main over FIVE other bodies is X=6, exactly 40 trample power into one seat, lethal with zero margin and only per-seat, never the pod (one of the five, Hornet Nest, has defender and never attacks — it raises X without swinging). Stack 005 also names the one card the deck's signature verb is wrong for: flashed on the prior end step, Craterhoof's +6/+6 and trample expire at that turn's cleanup (514.2), the swing is 10 unpumped power and it kills nobody; the flash mode is a wrath-dodge only. The four finishers are not one class. Only Craterhoof scales on creature COUNT and brings its own haste and trample; Overwhelming Stampede and Pathbreaker Ibex multiply by the greatest power on your board; Return of the Wildspeaker is a flat +3/+3 for NON-HUMAN creatures with no trample, and its other mode is a draw spell. Radagast's discount is creature-spell-only, so Craterhoof and Ibex can ride the window and Stampede (sorcery) and Return (instant) never can. This stage names no single point of failure: no passing stack resolves any of the other three, so nothing establishes either that they work or that they do not, and an open question asks.

v1_map_disagreements.component: A METRONOME body drawn (3-5 MV, >=2 generic — the full-value flash-in class)
v1_map_disagreements.why: Nineteen cards, five cities, 9/4/3/2/1. The class is defined by a COST BRACKET crossed with a permission printed on a different card. No member of it says anything about being a metronome body — they say 'draw a card', 'destroy target artifact', 'create a token' — so the map files each one under what it says. The law the scatter table demonstrates: a component is coherent on this map exactly when its defining property is printed on its members. THE OVERRUN KILL is 4-for-4 in one city because 'creatures you control get +X/+X' is the function; the metronome is invisible because the function lives on the commander.

v1_map_disagreements.component: A FLASH TRAP drawn (instant-speed interaction wearing a creature body, or held protection)
v1_map_disagreements.why: Sixteen cards, five cities, 6/5/3/1/1. The map splits cards that ARE instants (THE BODYGUARDS: Heroic Intervention, Veil of Summer, Tyvar's Stand) from cards the window MAKES into instants (THE TRAPS). The deck runs them as one class and pays for them with the same held mana. Whiptongue Hydra is the case in point: six mana, no printed flash, and the deck's premise card.

v1_map_disagreements.component: GAS drawn — a repeatable draw engine
v1_map_disagreements.why: Seven of ten sit in A CARD PER BODY, so this one is nearly coherent. The three strays each show the map choosing one of a card's two jobs: Selvala files under mana because she taps for it, Harmonize files under the wide board as a plain draw sorcery, and Toski files under armour because its printed text leads with indestructible and unblockable. Toski is the sharp one — the map reads a bodyguard, the deck runs a draw engine, and both readings are verified: stack 002 for the draw, stack 004 for the armour.

v1_map_disagreements.component: RAMP drawn (either hump: a dork/rock-class accelerant or a land-ramp spell)
v1_map_disagreements.why: Eighteen cards, four cities, 8/5/4/1 — and only PART of it is a disagreement. The declaration itself says 'either hump', and the map found exactly those two humps: dorks in MANA ON LEGS, land ramp in THE SEARCH PARTY. That much is agreement by design. The four in THE WIDE BOARD are the real split: Utopia Sprawl, Wild Growth and Fertile Ground cluster as enchantments rather than as mana, and Rampant Growth joins them. The one in GREEN ON CURVE is Castle Garenbrig, which is a land. A component that spans cities BY DESIGN is a different finding from one that spans them because its function is unwritten, and this component does both.

CORRECTED from iteration 1, which said this coupling sits in no city and called five cards its multipliers. FOUR cards read 'greatest power' and multiply by it — Overwhelming Stampede and Pathbreaker Ibex for their pump, Return of the Wildspeaker for both its modes (and its wording is 'greatest power among NON-HUMAN creatures you control'; the deck runs three Humans: Eternal Witness, Saryth and Sylvan Safekeeper), and Selvala for the size of her mana ability. A fifth card SETS the number rather than reading it: Mirkwood Pathmaker, whose power and toughness each equal your land count. Five cards in the coupling, four of them multipliers. No declared goldfish component groups them — that half of the iteration-1 claim stands. But the MAP has it four-fifths right: THE WIDE BOARD holds Stampede, Ibex, Return AND Pathmaker, and only Selvala strays to MANA ON LEGS. By this model's own coherence law that is nearly coherent, because 'greatest power among creatures you control' is printed on three of them. One thing the map cannot see and no component prices: Selvala's DRAW gate is 'if its power is greater than each other creature's power', which compares against opponents' creatures too — so a large Pathmaker may switch her draw trigger off for every subsequent body, and the coupling can run backwards.
